evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assay card. Input: viable single-cell suspension from tissue, blood or a suitable model, with cell identity and population gating documented. Routine fixed archival tissue cannot supply the starting living cells. Permeabilisation and peptide challenge consume the tested aliquots; cell demand depends on panel, controls and replicates rather than one universal tissue minimum. Output: named peptide response, dose, exposure time and population, reported as protocol-normalised depolarisation or cytochrome-c loss. Drug-minus-vehicle delta priming is in percentage points. evidence.supportingExcerpt: BH3 means BCL-2 homology 3. BAX and BAK can permeabilise the mitochondrial outer membrane, releasing cytochrome c from between the mitochondrial membranes into the cytosol. Priming concerns proximity to that threshold, not merely protein abundance. HRK-derived peptide preferentially probes BCL-XL, while BAD-derived peptide also challenges BCL-2 and BCL-W; overlapping patterns and concentrations matter. The assay peptide is not a vaccine-antigen recognition test. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2016.49

evidence.supportingExcerpt: BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1 oppose apoptosis, whereas other family members promote it; a BH3 region is a protein region participating in this signalling. A larger mitochondrial response to the same defined challenge can indicate greater priming, and cytochrome-c release helps initiate downstream death machinery. Strong protein staining alone does not establish functional dependence. Butterworth compared peptide profiles with selective BH3-mimetic inhibitors: using both was more informative when survival involved multiple anti-apoptotic proteins, so discordant readouts warrant investigation. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/bjc.2016.49

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Normalisation and failure checks. In the Ryan and Letai potential-dye protocol, vehicle and a depolarising control define the assay range: subtract the depolarising-control signal from the sample and vehicle signals. Divide the sample difference by the vehicle difference, subtract that ratio from one and multiply by 100 to obtain percent depolarisation. This is not an absolute percentage of dead cells. In cytochrome-c protocols, read retained or lost signal against the specified controls and gating convention; do not interchange fluorescence retention and release. Poor baseline viability, damaged mitochondria, excessive permeabilisation, wrong cell identity, loss of tumour populations or saturated responses can invalidate comparison. Thresholds are protocol- and study-specific. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-8861-7_4

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assay card. Input: viable single-cell suspension from tissue, blood or a suitable model, with cell identity and population gating documented. Routine fixed archival tissue cannot supply the starting living cells. Permeabilisation and peptide challenge consume the tested aliquots; cell demand depends on panel, controls and replicates rather than one universal tissue minimum. Output: named peptide response, dose, exposure time and population, reported as protocol-normalised depolarisation or cytochrome-c loss. Drug-minus-vehicle delta priming is in percentage points. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-8861-7_4

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Normalisation and failure checks. In the Ryan and Letai potential-dye protocol, vehicle and a depolarising control define the assay range: subtract the depolarising-control signal from the sample and vehicle signals. Divide the sample difference by the vehicle difference, subtract that ratio from one and multiply by 100 to obtain percent depolarisation. This is not an absolute percentage of dead cells. In cytochrome-c protocols, read retained or lost signal against the specified controls and gating convention; do not interchange fluorescence retention and release. Poor baseline viability, damaged mitochondria, excessive permeabilisation, wrong cell identity, loss of tumour populations or saturated responses can invalidate comparison. Thresholds are protocol- and study-specific. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006 ; https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-8861-7_4

evidence.supportingExcerpt: BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1 oppose apoptosis, whereas other family members promote it; a BH3 region is a protein region participating in this signalling. evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional dynamic-profiling experiment, cells pre-exposed to vehicle show 20 percent normalised depolarisation when given a peptide, and cells pre-exposed to the drug show 55 percent for the same peptide. (In the normalisation, peptide-free vehicle wells define 0 percent and the depolarising control defines 100 percent; the 20 percent belongs to vehicle-pre-exposed cells challenged with the peptide.) The increase is 35 percentage points, not a 35 percent killed-cell fraction, a causal variant finding or a safe treatment. Values can exceed 100 percent in the potential-dye protocol, so the scale must not be read as a literal cell-death fraction. Source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymeth.2013.04.006

requirement: Bioprinting = controlled deposition of cells, biomaterials or both to build a planned structure for a biological experiment.
sourceUnitDescription: Bioprinting = controlled deposition of cells, biomaterials or both to build a planned structure for a biological experiment.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Model card. Input: defined cells and biomaterials, sometimes viable patient-derived material requiring expansion. Document the source of each component; patient-derived tumour cells do not make every material donor-matched. Fabrication and quality checks consume finite material. Output: measured geometry in micrometres or millimetres, viability or attributed counts, and the separately chosen functional endpoint. Retain actual layout, matrix, cell identities, time and controls; a digital plan is not the final measurement. A printing plan specifies positions, materials and fabrication steps. A bioink is a formulation used to build a biological construct, often containing cells in a supportive material. The extracellular matrix is the surrounding molecular scaffold of tissue; a printing material represents selected features rather than its whole composition. A sacrificial ink is temporary material removed to leave a channel. Some designs deposit cells with the material; another route builds a support that is seeded afterwards. Gelation, adding cell populations and making channels are distinct steps. Kolesky's cell-laden and fugitive-ink method is one documented implementation, rather than proof of every possible printing route. Source: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1521342113

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Bioprinting controls deposition of biological materials to build an experimental construct. The printing plan, measured final geometry, viable cells and biological function are distinct evidence. Kolesky and colleagues printed cell-containing and removable inks, removed the temporary channel material, added endothelial lining and perfused engineered tissues. This tissue-engineering experiment did not demonstrate a complete human organ or cancer-treatment utility. Yi and colleagues reported a particular glioblastoma chip combining patient-derived tumour cells, endothelial cells and brain-derived matrix; its abstract supports that bounded example.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Channel checks. A temporary channel path becomes a hollow channel after removal; endothelial lining, fluid passage and barrier performance require separate tests. Kolesky's primary figures distinguish these steps and compare diffusional permeability of lined and bare channels. Printing describes fabrication; a chip describes an environment, while organoid self-organisation describes another design axis. More complex fabrication does not automatically validate prediction. Living cells can spread, contract and remodel the initial layout. The actual geometry and cell health therefore need observation after printing as well as a design file. In Kolesky's primary PDF, figures 1 and 2 separate fabrication, viability, endothelial lining and measured permeability of lined versus bare channels. Those checks support those engineered tissues, not a complete organ. Perfusion supplies fluid through the constructed system; it is not full human circulation or drug metabolism.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Model and assay card. Record viable cell/tissue sources, matrix, channel geometry, material, flow or exchange conditions, barrier performance, loading losses and quality window. Preparation, loading and endpoint assays use finite material. Report the actual endpoint and units: attributed counts or death, permeability, cytokine concentration or motion, with time and denominator. Verify initial composition, baseline survival and local exposure; incompatible materials, unequal delivery and poor barriers can confound results. Device and assay acceptance criteria are method-specific. A chip may combine bioprinting, organoids or co-culture without recreating complete circulation. Microfluidics controls fluid in small channels. Perfusion supplies fluid through a system; it does not itself recreate human circulation or prove a functional vascular lining. Immune cells, if present, still need recognition and attribution controls. A tumour-on-chip is a living experimental device, whereas an in-silico model computes predictions. A device without the required immune cells cannot test their checkpoint interaction. Cells can alter the engineered environment, so both the design and its measured biological state matter; added detail alone does not establish better prediction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Model card. Input: documented banked cells or viable material used to establish a culture. Record source and version, medium, density, passage and relevant phenotype. Output belongs to the chosen assay, such as counts, doubling time in hours or a death fraction with its denominator. Passage counts transfers, not a fixed number of divisions. Identity matching by human short tandem repeat profiling, mycoplasma testing and phenotype/growth checks address different questions. Establishment can fail or select subsets; no line-name cutoff predicts clinical sensitivity. Sources: https://www.atcc.org/resources/culture-guides/animal-cell-culture-guide ; https://www.atcc.org/-/media/resources/technical-documents/cell-line-authentication-test-recommendations.pdf?rev=7664fa886e5948018dfe198d484bb4eb Establishing a new line uses finite viable tissue and can select populations. A cell line need not be a monolayer. ATCC uses authentication broadly for verification of identity and freedom from contamination: short tandem repeat profiling compares repeated DNA stretches to test human-line identity, while mycoplasma and other contamination tests and relevant phenotype checks answer additional questions. Passing the identity test does not answer all of them.

A cell line need not be a monolayer. ATCC uses authentication broadly for verification of identity and freedom from contamination: short tandem repeat profiling compares repeated DNA stretches to test human-line identity, while mycoplasma and other contamination tests and relevant phenotype checks answer additional questions. Passing the identity test does not answer all of them.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Dijkstra primary study: a two-week enrichment stage preceded a separate three-day organoid-killing assessment. Matched healthy organoids and HLA-blocking comparisons tested specificity; reactions to xenogeneic Geltrex matrix were also investigated. A marker or cytokine signal alone did not substitute for the identified live-cell/death readout. The studied donors and protocol define the scope: the colorectal samples were mismatch repair-deficient, and the defined T-cell response occurred in four of eight patients with MHC class I-positive organoids in the colorectal comparison. No response was observed in the tested MHC class I-deficient lines. These timings are not universal culture windows. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/ Jenkins also described organotypic spheroids retaining autologous immune and stromal components. Added blood lymphocytes and retained tumour neighbours are different preparations; measure retention and function over the actual window rather than assign immune capability exclusively to one format. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional mixed culture, a metabolic signal falls by half, but identified viable tumour-cell counts are unchanged and viable immune-cell counts fall. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Dijkstra primary study: a two-week enrichment stage preceded a separate three-day organoid-killing assessment. Matched healthy organoids and HLA-blocking comparisons tested specificity; reactions to xenogeneic Geltrex matrix were also investigated. A marker or cytokine signal alone did not substitute for the identified live-cell/death readout. The studied donors and protocol define the scope: the colorectal samples were mismatch repair-deficient, and the defined T-cell response occurred in four of eight patients with MHC class I-positive organoids in the colorectal comparison. No response was observed in the tested MHC class I-deficient lines. These timings are not universal culture windows. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/ Jenkins also described organotypic spheroids retaining autologous immune and stromal components. Added blood lymphocytes and retained tumour neighbours are different preparations; measure retention and function over the actual window rather than assign immune capability exclusively to one format. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/

requirement: Distinguish a genetic dependency from drug inhibition and safe treatment, including compensation and alternative protein forms.
sourceUnitDescription: Removing-a-gear analogy: dependency does not say whether a particular brake can slow it safely; genetic disruption vs drug inhibition differ; cells compensate, use alternative protein forms, change state.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: On-target follow-up is a reading rule: check the edit and functional consequence, reproduce the effect with independent guides or another suitable perturbation, and test whether restoration of the relevant function reverses the phenotype where feasible. Rescue has its own expression and construct controls; failed rescue alone is not proof against the target. This is a causal-comparison framework, not a claim that every published screen performed all these experiments. Responses can include compensation, alternative protein forms or changes in cellular state. Mou reported exon skipping and exon deletions after CRISPR editing, while El-Brolosy studied mutant-mRNA-dependent transcriptional adaptation in zebrafish and mouse models. These bounded findings explain why the resulting RNA, protein and phenotype need checking; they do not establish a universal frequency of compensation. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-017-1237-8 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1064-z

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In pooled CRISPR knockout screens, guide sequences track perturbed populations over time. Relative enrichment or depletion supports a fitness effect under the experimental conditions, including proliferation and survival. Guide delivery and editing efficiency, representation, unintended effects and copy-number-dependent cutting can confound interpretation. Independent perturbations and appropriate follow-up strengthen on-target attribution. Knockout and drug inhibition differ in extent, activity and duration, so a genetic hit does not establish a clinically useful drug.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Analysis scope. CERES estimates genetic effects while accounting for copy-number cutting effects. Chronos models perturbed population dynamics and was compared with other methods on two pan-cancer datasets and a longitudinal screen. Its reported control separation and bias advantages belong to those comparisons; correction does not make a poor experiment valid. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709193/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-021-02540-7 Cutting several amplified copies can impair growth through DNA damage independently of losing the targeted gene function. In a fictional barcode example, a guide falling from 100 to 20 reads per 10,000 reads has decreased in relative representation; it does not mean that 80 cells died. Proliferation, survival, editing and cutting effects need the separate checks described here.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some dependencies are shared broadly and others enriched in a particular lineage or genomic context. A gene needed by normal cells may limit therapeutic selectivity. Knockout can remove a protein, whereas a drug may inhibit only one activity partly or temporarily. Guide abundance after perturbation is not RNA expression, and a negative gene-effect score follows the analysis convention rather than guaranteeing drug sensitivity. No screen alone establishes normal-tissue safety. In a fictional amplified-region example, a strong depletion signal becomes small after cutting-toxicity correction; the original rank alone cannot nominate an inhibitor. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709193/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: On-target follow-up is a reading rule: check the edit and functional consequence, reproduce the effect with independent guides or another suitable perturbation, and test whether restoration of the relevant function reverses the phenotype where feasible. Rescue has its own expression and construct controls; failed rescue alone is not proof against the target. This is a causal-comparison framework, not a claim that every published screen performed all these experiments. Responses can include compensation, alternative protein forms or changes in cellular state. Mou reported exon skipping and exon deletions after CRISPR editing, while El-Brolosy studied mutant-mRNA-dependent transcriptional adaptation in zebrafish and mouse models. These bounded findings explain why the resulting RNA, protein and phenotype need checking; they do not establish a universal frequency of compensation. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-017-1237-8 ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1064-z

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In pooled CRISPR knockout screens, guide sequences track perturbed populations over time. Relative enrichment or depletion supports a fitness effect under the experimental conditions, including proliferation and survival. Guide delivery and editing efficiency, representation, unintended effects and copy-number-dependent cutting can confound interpretation. Independent perturbations and appropriate follow-up strengthen on-target attribution. Knockout and drug inhibition differ in extent, activity and duration, so a genetic hit does not establish a clinically useful drug.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-022-04025-0

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Endpoint and validation example. Ladan reported 23 usable assays among 30 tumour-containing biopsies; three of the 23 did not proceed to the clinical treatment comparison, leaving 20 evaluable patients and 15 concordant MRI comparisons. The agreement compared sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories after four courses of anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; it is not a binary drug-killing rate. The study did not observe an ex vivo resistant group, limiting assessment of resistance detection. Those denominators, assay version and preoperative setting cannot validate another postoperative choice. Salmon measured matrix-associated T-cell location and movement in viable lung-tumour slices, not treatment-selection benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Regulatory scope. FDA's roadmap to reduce animal testing concerns preclinical safety development, initially focusing on monoclonal antibodies and considering human-based laboratory and computational methods. It is not approval of every organ chip or a recommendation for personal treatment selection. Source: https://www.fda.gov/files/newsroom/published/roadmap_to_reducing_animal_testing_in_preclinical_safety_studies.pdf Decision time limits which preparation is usable: establishing a new conventional PDX generally will not fit a decision due in three weeks, while a characterised short-term assay might fit but can still fail. A treatment needing liver activation also needs the relevant metabolic setting represented; a fresh slice alone omits it. Computation can rank hypotheses without growing a model, but a universal fastest or cheapest claim is not established by the setting label.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Primary timing examples. Ladan's breast-slice assay used three-day exposures, a stated planned result window of seven to fourteen days, not a measured turnaround distribution and 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 established PDXs and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to exposure, not biopsy to final decision. Ahlmann-Eltze compared gene-perturbation transcriptome predictions with simple baselines; the deep-learning methods did not outperform the simple linear baselines in the tested expression-prediction tasks. This was not a measured patient drug response. None of these examples shows benefit from choosing a treatment using the model. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40759747/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. No preparation is universally more predictive because it is more complex. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2018.11.021 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Construction and readout. Record source and identity, retained or added populations, viable window, preparation/version and missing components. Define measured or predicted object, units, reference and uncertainty. Check relevant controls, baseline growth and population attribution. A lower count than a dividing control is not necessarily a count below the start. Reliability within a run, independent biological specimens and correctness answer different questions. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ Human-derived cells or tissue are not complete human physiology. Repeatability can preserve a systematic error; a measured treatment effect does not identify its mechanism without comparisons that distinguish alternative explanations.

The question, retained components, exposure, readout and comparison against relevant observations should accompany a model claim.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional example. A tumour-only culture repeatedly responds to Drug A. This does not test an immune-dependent Drug B or prove benefit because the cells came from a patient. Check the required immune interaction, actual intervention, endpoint and independent validation. Repeatability cannot repair a mismatch between question and model. These are invented drugs and a reading exercise. Complexity is useful when it represents biology necessary for the question and remains measurable. A simpler model may isolate a mechanism, while another model is needed for an interaction absent from it. More components alone do not show better prediction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Failure and inference checks. Establishment can fail, normal epithelial cells can overgrow malignant cells, and culture conditions can select branches. Verify tumour identity rather than infer it from growth. Output belongs to the chosen assay: attributed cell counts, death-marker fraction or molecular signal, with units, time and normalisation. Check viability, composition, exposure and controls. A three-dimensional spheroid need not show tissue-like self-organisation, and specialised immune retention does not apply to all cultures. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10598932/ Dijkstra explicitly checked tumour identity to exclude healthy-lung organoid overgrowth: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Size, matrix, oxygen supply and exposure duration belong in the experiment record because they define conditions for delivery, cell state and the readout. As a bounded example, Geyer's pancreatic organoid study found treatment-response differences between normoxia and hypoxia in specified monocultures and co-cultures. evidence.supportingExcerpt: DeStefanis and colleagues tracked nearly 3,500 individual mouse-derived colon-cancer organoids. In that model, organoids at or above a change point of about 308 micrometres at baseline grew more slowly, and individual-organoid tracking was reported to be more sensitive to treatment response than well-level assessment, which averages the whole population in a well. In their 1,740 patient-derived organoids (22 lines, 19 patients) they found no relation between baseline size and growth (R squared 0.023) and no change point in any line. These are findings of one study and model, not a universal size threshold. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-08937-z

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

Whole-animal dosing includes mouse exposure and metabolism, not human physiology. Humanised models add selected components whose identity, compatibility and persistence need checking. Fidelity and patient prediction are question- and method-specific.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Throughput and repetition depend on how material can be expanded. A xenograft can be passaged into further mice, but each drug comparison needs suitable animals and controls. An established organoid line can be expanded and passaged to compare a drug panel; Sachs reported retention of many source features during extended passaging, not unlimited fidelity. A cut piece has a finite culture window and a limited number of matched conditions; it cannot simply be expanded while retaining the same original neighbourhood. Ladan's group described viability for up to a week. These are practical preparation contrasts, not a universal numerical throughput ranking or an assumption that every organoid survives freezing. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-022-04025-0

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The clocks and take rates below belong to different studies. Hidalgo's review described four to eight months to a study-ready PDX. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 establishment and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with tumour-type variation: 85 percent in colorectal specimens and 30 percent in breast specimens in that series. Cartry reported a 61.5 percent core-biopsy take rate and six-week median, range four to ten weeks, to a 25-drug colorectal organoid panel. Boileve reported 54/87 establishment (62 percent) and mean 6.8 weeks to a pancreatic chemogram. Ladan used three-day exposures and stated that results can be known in seven to fourteen days; this is a planned window, not an observed turnaround distribution. There were 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. The PDX paper reports 49 percent for 578/1,163; direct count arithmetic is approximately 49.7 percent.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assay card. Input: viable cells compatible with suspension and channel handling. Record source, identity, preparation losses, fluid and temperature conditions, exposure and observation interval. Calibration maps frequency shifts to mass, often picograms. Tracking repeated readings estimates a slope, often picograms per hour; mass-normalised rates have inverse-time units. Preparation and exposure consume finite material; the physical measurement can preserve cells, but recovery and downstream compatibility depend on the method.

sourceUnitDescription: Tumor-on-chip = engineered culture device to study selected tumor-tissue interactions under defined physical/biological conditions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Model and assay card. Record viable cell/tissue sources, matrix, channel geometry, material, flow or exchange conditions, barrier performance, loading losses and quality window. Preparation, loading and endpoint assays use finite material. Report the actual endpoint and units: attributed counts or death, permeability, cytokine concentration or motion, with time and denominator. Verify initial composition, baseline survival and local exposure; incompatible materials, unequal delivery and poor barriers can confound results. Device and assay acceptance criteria are method-specific. A chip may combine bioprinting, organoids or co-culture without recreating complete circulation. Microfluidics controls fluid in small channels. Perfusion supplies fluid through a system; it does not itself recreate human circulation or prove a functional vascular lining. Immune cells, if present, still need recognition and attribution controls. A tumour-on-chip is a living experimental device, whereas an in-silico model computes predictions. A device without the required immune cells cannot test their checkpoint interaction. Cells can alter the engineered environment, so both the design and its measured biological state matter; added detail alone does not establish better prediction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Geometry and exposure. A porous interface, a perfused channel and a tissue compartment are separate features. In Huh's design, a membrane separated epithelial and endothelial layers and vacuum channels imposed deformation. Jenkins used collagen containing spheroids in a central channel. These geometries must not be silently interchanged. A fictional one-micromolar inlet illustrates a reading rule: concentration at an inlet is not a measurement at each cell. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8335790/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5809290/ One micromolar means one micromole per litre; it is the nominal inlet value in this example, not a measured cellular exposure.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Model and assay card. Record viable cell/tissue sources, matrix, channel geometry, material, flow or exchange conditions, barrier performance, loading losses and quality window. Preparation, loading and endpoint assays use finite material. Report the actual endpoint and units: attributed counts or death, permeability, cytokine concentration or motion, with time and denominator. Verify initial composition, baseline survival and local exposure; incompatible materials, unequal delivery and poor barriers can confound results. Device and assay acceptance criteria are method-specific. A chip may combine bioprinting, organoids or co-culture without recreating complete circulation. Microfluidics controls fluid in small channels. Perfusion supplies fluid through a system; it does not itself recreate human circulation or prove a functional vascular lining. Immune cells, if present, still need recognition and attribution controls. A tumour-on-chip is a living experimental device, whereas an in-silico model computes predictions. A device without the required immune cells cannot test their checkpoint interaction. Cells can alter the engineered environment, so both the design and its measured biological state matter; added detail alone does not establish better prediction.
